title: Adaptive reference-set expansion and temperature-aware judge calibration
creator: Marco Reyes
description: Problem: We observe brittle regression signals when rolling config/model changes because our fixed reference set and single-temperature LLM-as-judge produce cohort-specific bias and noisy deltas. Goal: make regression detection stable across cohorts and model variants by (1) dynamically expanding the reference set with stratified sampling and automated anchor selection, and (2) calibrating the LLM-as-judge output temperature and decision thresholds per cohort so score deltas map to meaningful effect sizes.
background: Current eval pipeline uses a static reference set (10k prompts) and a single rubric + default judge temperature. Recent rollouts produced false positives localized to long-form summarization and code generation cohorts. Pager noise increases SLO churn and slows safe rollouts. Engineering has instrumented cohort tags and bootstrap sampling in ENG-2784; PM needs a methodology to combine these signals into robust regression alerts and rollout gates.
proposal: 1) Reference-set expansion: implement a rolling reference update process that adds stratified samples from live traffic and synthetic edge cases. Each weekly snapshot will keep 70% stable anchors and 30% rotating candidates. Anchors are selected by cross-validated human agreement scores. 2) Temperature-aware judge calibration: for each cohort and model/config variant, run a small calibration sweep (temperatures 0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0) and choose the temperature that optimizes AUC against human-labeled anchors. Persist temperature selection in eval metadata and apply at eval runtime. 3) Effect-size thresholds: translate judge-score deltas into Cohen's d-style effect sizes using within-cohort variance, and set alert thresholds that require both statistical significance and minimum effect size to trigger rollout blocks. 4) Backfill & migration: backfill new reference snapshots over the past 6 weeks and re-run historical rollouts to recalibrate thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline can produce per-cohort judge temperatures and reference snapshots for each weekly eval run
False-positive regression rate for historical 10 recent rollouts reduced by >=50% compared to baseline
Alerting UI surfaces cohort, temperature, anchor examples, effect-size, and human agreement metrics
New thresholds integrated with rollout gating so canary blocks require both p-value < 0.01 and Cohen's d >= 0.25
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement reference-set rotation framework and storage schema; add cohort stratification hooks. Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement calibration runner to sweep temperatures, compute AUC against anchors, and persist chosen temperature. Phase 3 (1 week): compute effect-size translation and update alert thresholds; expose metadata in console. Phase 4 (1 week): backfill last 6 weeks and run QA against historical rollouts. Blockers: stable human anchor labeling process and infra to run calibration sweeps in parallel without impacting prod tokens.
rollout_plan: Start behind feature flag. Enable for non-critical cohorts first (search snippets, short responses) and monitor false-positive rate. If stable after 2 weeks, enable for high-risk cohorts. Integrate with rollout gating so rollout UI shows recommended action (proceed/hold) with the calibrations and anchors visible.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for reference selection logic and seed determinism. 2) Simulated regression injection tests using synthetic degradations to verify alerting behavior. 3) Human-in-the-loop validation: sample 200 anchor judgments per cohort and compute judge vs human AUC. 4) Canary run: apply to one active canary rollout and compare against baseline pipeline for two weeks.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Judge temperature overfitting to anchors -> Mitigation: cross-validate using K-fold and require minimum generalization AUC
Risk: Increased compute overhead for calibration sweeps -> Mitigation: budgeted parallelism and caching of intermediate embeddings; run calibration on sampled subset
Risk: Anchor label drift over time -> Mitigation: rotate anchors slowly and schedule periodic human review cycles
